newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen continuing weaker at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen continuing weaker at open.

* Toronto's stocks were expected to lose further ground at the open as election jitters set in. * Traders said polls showing decreased support for Liberals have made investors skittish.
Toronto stocks were expected to lose further ground at the open on Wednesday and traders said the market would remain volatile ahead of Monday's federal election.
"The market probably will be a little weaker today at the opening...with the election coming up and the polls the way they are, we're skittish," one trader said.

Analysts said recent polls showing a decreasing lead for Canada's governing Liberals ahead of the June 2 general election were adding volatility to currency trading which was in turn dragging down bonds, bills and stocks.

"The other concern is it's not just that the Liberals are slipping but the Reform, there's a real risk of Reform forming the opposition...the risk is if Preston Manning really presses it about the Quebec situation, the Quebec situation comes back to the front of everybody's attention, which will hurt the Canadian dollar, and in turn all our markets," said technical analyst Katherine Beattie at MMS International.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index finished 48.59 points lower on Tuesday at 6442.54 after a record-setting rally in the days earlier.
Heavyweight financial issues generally lost ground after the first two of the big six banks reported record second quarter earnings which matched analysts' expectations.
Beattie said weak bond and bill markets hurt the banks in what might have been a stong post-earnings session.
In economic news, Canada's raw materials price index fell 1.1 percent in April from March, while the April industrial price index rose 0.5 percent from a month earlier.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---
* Royal Bank of Canada, Canada's largest, was expected to report second quarter results later in the session.
